intended_object: Take a multilinear map f, a point m and an index i. The intended object is the linear map in the i-th variable, x ↦ f(m with its i-th coordinate replaced by x), obtained by holding every other coordinate fixed at m. This comes from the docstring.
explanation: The body defines the map as `x ↦ f (update m i x)`, which is exactly "fix every coordinate except the i-th and vary the i-th one". Additivity and compatibility with scalars follow from `map_update_add` and `map_update_smul`, which are the axioms of a multilinear map. The setting is as general as the notion: a semiring R, any index type ι, and modules M₁ i and M₂ that are additive commutative monoids. `DecidableEq ι` is the standard requirement for `Function.update`. This is the Mathlib declaration itself, and I know of no other declaration that defines the same object in more generality.
